english: A data set consists of the observation $6$ occurring once, $12$ occurring $4$ times, $16$ occurring $k$ times and $25$ occurring $4$ times, where $k$ is a positive integer. The same data are grouped into the classes $[0,10),[10,20),[20,30)$. The ungrouped data have a unique mode, and this mode is equal to the mode of the grouped frequency distribution. hindi: एक आँकड़ा समुच्चय में प्रेक्षण $6$ एक बार, $12$ चार बार, $16$ $k$ बार तथा $25$ चार बार आता है, जहाँ $k$ एक धनात्मक पूर्णांक है। इन्हीं आँकड़ों को वर्गों $[0,10),[10,20),[20,30)$ में समूहित किया जाता है। अवर्गीकृत आँकड़ों का एक अद्वितीय बहुलक है तथा यह बहुलक समूहित बारंबारता बंटन के बहुलक के बराबर है। तब $k$ बराबर है
solution: Unique ungrouped mode: if $k\le4$, the value $12$ or $25$ ties for the top, so $k\ge5$ and the mode is $16$
solution_full: If $k\le4$, then $12$ and $25$ both occur $4$ times and no value occurs more often, so the mode is not unique. Hence $k\ge5$, and the unique mode is $16$.
Check: frequencies $1,10,4$ give $10+\dfrac{9}{15}\cdot10=16$, and $16$ occurs $6$ times, more than any other value.
originality_note: New: one data set is read twice, as raw values (unique mode) and as a grouped table (interpolated mode), and the two modes are required to agree, which fixes an unknown frequency (way 3: an object fixed by two conditions). Closest known: missing-frequency problems with a given grouped mode. Different because: the target value of the mode is not given; it comes from the uniqueness condition on the raw data.
stem_review: Read as a student: every observation, class, symbol and condition is introduced before use, the class-boundary convention is explicit where it matters, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (exact fractions / sympy), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked k = 1..14: only k = 6 satisfies both conditions (k = 4 gives three modes). Changed: chose frequencies so that the modal class is the same for every k.
key_step: Using the uniqueness of the raw mode to get the target value 16, then solving the grouped-mode formula for k.
justification: Two ideas linked (raw mode with a uniqueness case, grouped mode formula). Above the one-table L2 statistics anchors (2025-P1-Q14) because the condition must first be decoded. Borderline 2/3.

concept_use.Mode of ungrouped data: Uniqueness of the raw mode forces k >= 5 and makes the mode 16.
concept_use.Mode of a continuous frequency distribut: The grouped mode l + (f1 - f0) h / (2 f1 - f0 - f2) with f1 = 4 + k is set equal to 16.
